title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and set the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw a two-dimensional sketch consisting of a loop with six lines. Start by drawing the first line from the origin at zero, zero to zero point zero two seven eight, zero. Continue with the second line from zero point zero two seven eight, zero to zero point zero two seven eight, zero point zero two seven eight. Draw the third line from zero point zero two seven eight, zero point zero two seven eight to zero point zero two six one, zero point zero two seven eight. The fourth line should go from zero point zero two six one, zero point zero two seven eight to zero point zero two six one, zero point zero zero one seven. Draw the fifth line from zero point zero two six one, zero point zero zero one seven to zero, zero point zero zero one seven. Finally, draw the sixth line from zero, zero point zero zero one seven back to the origin at zero, zero. Apply a scaling factor of zero point zero two seven eight to the two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the sketch zero point seven five units in the direction of the normal to create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the part are a length of zero point zero two seven eight units, a width of zero point zero two seven eight units, and a height of zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0278, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0278, 0.0278) \
     .lineTo(0.0261, 0.0278) \
     .lineTo(0.0261, 0.0017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r = r

# Display the model

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-angle profile: horizontal leg along Y, vertical leg along Z
L = 0.7500   # length along X
W = 0.0278   # width of horizontal leg (along Y)
H = 0.0278   # height of vertical leg (along Z)
T = 0.0055   # wall thickness

# Sketch the L cross-section in the YZ plane and extrude along X
profile = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(W, 0)
    .lineTo(W, T)
    .lineTo(T, T)
    .lineTo(T, H)
    .lineTo(0, H)
    .close()
    .extrude(L)
)

r = profile

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-shaped angle profile (equal legs 0.0278 x 0.0278) extruded along X
w = 0.0278      # leg width (Y and Z)
t = 0.0035      # wall thickness
L = 0.75        # length along X

profile = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(w, 0)
    .lineTo(w, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, w)
    .lineTo(0, w)
    .close()
)

r = profile.extrude(L)
